text:
maya: Quick snapshot — after the kernel-affinity rollout to kernel-k4 for rtx-2 models we see a sharp drop in prefetch hit-line on /summarize and /chat/paraphrase routes. Noting per-token savings fell ~40% for a handful of tenants. Putting numbers below and tagging for triage.

perf-bot: automated-metrics: prefetch_hit_rate (global, top routes): before=0.46, after=0.28, delta=-0.18. token_saved_rate: before=320k/day, after=190k/day. 90th p95 latency change: +12ms. Affected model: rtx-2-2026-q4. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/prefetch/hitline?run=5177777777

arjun: hmm. kernel-affinity changed how kernels pick packers/quant paths. Could be key-normalizer rounding differences -> different key derivation. Did we change any prompt-normalization flags in the rollout?

maya: not intentionally. rollout notes: "kernel-k4: pick packer v2, faster fused-kv copy; no prompt-normalizer change". But the runtime switched to a new batching heuristic that pads sequences differently.

joel: can we get a per-tenant breakdown? If it's just a few tenants with stable seed prompts then key skew might explain it.

perf-bot: per-tenant top-5 impact (prefetch_hit_rate delta): tenant-acme: -0.42, tenant-borealis: -0.35, tenant-middleman: -0.05, tenant-sandbox: +0.02, tenant-edgecase: -0.61. Only ~6% of total accounts account for 70% of token-savings regression.

kim: ops, can we roll the kernel-affinity back for the small cohort while we debug? Canary windows? @ops

ops: I can pin the earlier kernel-k3 for pool arena-3 and arena-5 for affected tenants. ETA ~15m for a rollback + warmup. Will schedule a short canary.

arjun: Meanwhile, run this quick query to compare normalized prompt keys pre/post: ```
-- compare prompt key fingerprints by prefix
SELECT prefix_hash, count(*) as cnt, avg(seq_len) as avg_len
FROM prompt_keys
WHERE model = 'rtx-2-2026-q4' AND ts BETWEEN 5177700000 AND 5177777000
GROUP BY prefix_hash
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

maya: good. Also capture KV-cache hit latency distribution and KV cache get/set payload sizes. If kernels change packing, KV key serialization might differ.

perf-bot: note: key-normalizer pipeline shows 0.3% new-normalization hits after rollout (expansion of whitespace handling). That might be enough for heavy tenants.

joel: we should also profile batch packing behavior for short vs long sequences. Kernel-k4's packer might group short requests differently, causing different prefix chunking. I'll run a trace sampling for the next 30m with batch-size histogram.

kim: +1 to profiling. Also run kv-warmup delta: how many warmed keys were evicted during the rollout window? If warmup misses spiked, that'll reduce hit-rate.

perf-bot: kv-warmup evictions: window pre=12k/h warmed_keys, post=48k/h evicted_keys. Correlation with kernel change flagged (p<0.01).

sre-bot: alert context: no infra failures, memory and GPU utilization steady. This looks functional (keying/packing) rather than capacity. Putting a low-priority incident note.

maya: action list I'm going to drive: 1) ops rollback targeted pools (kim & ops) 2) arjun/joel to run key-fingerprint diffs + batch packing traces 3) perf to produce per-route token-saved waterfall (perf-bot) 4) add regression test to CI that asserts no >0.1 drop in prefetch hitline for our top-10 tenant workload.

arjun: one more thought — kernel-k4 introduced a new tiny-optimizer that strips trailing nul bytes from serialized keys to reduce kernel memcpy. If some normalizer relied on those bytes, key identity changes. I'll inspect the kernel change list.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (detailed): routes: /summarize: hitrate pre=0.52 post=0.31, /chat/paraphrase: pre=0.47 post=0.25; token_saved delta by model: rtx-2-2026-q4: -130k/day, rtx-2-2026-q3: -8k/day.

joel: started trace sampling -> collecting 2k batches, will post artifacts link in thread.

ops: rollback started on arena-3. Warmup in progress. Will monitor hitline panels; will post update at +30m.

maya: if rollback restores hitline we'll pin kernel-k3 for the affected fleets and roll k4 back for a wider pause. If not, deeper key-normalizer debugging next. Thanks all — please post TL;DRs in thread as you have them. :thumbsup:
